name: ai_novm_computer

phase_0.boundary_condition: the normalization constraint ∑E_i = I_d — every NOVM operator set must resolve the identity, bounding the measurement outcomes to total probability one

VINIT.justification: the tool starts with no parameters loaded, no operators allocated, no state specified — void before any measurement structure is constructed

TANCH.chosen_element: normalization constraint ∑E_i = I_d established as boundary
TANCH.justification: the identity-resolution condition is set as the closed container for all subsequent operations — no operator construction may violate this sum-to-identity closure

AFWD.justification: forward morphism transforms the input parameters (d, m, negativity strength α, asymmetry vector) into concrete Hermitian operators {E_i} using the generalized Gell-Mann basis with parameterized negativity, ensuring each operator is self-adjoint

AREV.chosen_element: eigenvalue decomposition E_i = U_i Λ_i U_i†
AREV.justification: reverse morphism decomposes each constructed operator into its spectral form — the descent from matrix to eigenvalues, producing the minimal eigenvalue λ_min(i) and the full spectrum needed for property verification

CLINK.justification: sequential composition chains the tool output into the Imscribing Grammar catalog — the JSON output links to the asymmetric_ai_novm entry, enabling distance computations and crystal navigation on the result

IMSCRIB.justification: identity verification confirms each operator equals its adjoint — the self-reference of a Hermitian matrix, required for real-valued quasi-probabilities and valid spectral decomposition

FSPLIT.justification: co-multiplication splits the identity operator I_d into the set of m Hermitian operators {E_1, ..., E_m} — each operator is a branch of the resolution of identity, with the construction guaranteeing ∑E_i = I_d

FFUSE.justification: multiplication fuses all m operators via summation ∑E_i, recovering exactly I_d — the NOVM normalization condition guarantees closure, and the fuse_result I_d is identical to the split_input I_d, satisfying the Frobenius constraint

EVALT.justification: affirmative evaluation — the operator set passes the current property check: negativity eigenvalue found (λ_min < 0 for some operator), incompleteness confirmed (m < d²), or asymmetry verified (all spectra distinct)

EVALF.justification: negative evaluation — the operator set fails the current property: all eigenvalues nonnegative (standard POVM), operators span the full operator space (tomographically complete), or spectra not distinct (symmetry group present)

ENGAGR.justification: both states held simultaneously — the Born rule output (p_1, ..., p_m) is both a valid measurement distribution (∑p_i = 1 per the NOVM normalization) and an invalid classical probability (some p_i < 0); this paradice is the defining signature of negative operator valued measures

IFIX.justification: permanent irreversible record — the quasi-probability vector, negativity quantification N(ρ), verification results, operator spectra, and grammar tuple ⟨𐑨𐑰𐑽𐑗𐑐𐑪𐑲𐑠𐑢𐑒𐑳𐑷⟩ are written to a fixed JSON artifact for downstream consumption by the grammar pipeline

phase_2.split_input: the identity operator I_d on ℂ^d
split_outputs: the set of m Hermitian operators {E_1, ..., E_m}
the NOVM resolution of identity with ∑E_i = I_d by construction
phase_2.fuse_result: the identity operator I_d on ℂ^d

phase_3.void_description: uninitialized tool — no parameters specified, no operators allocated, no state loaded; the tool awaits dimension d, outcome count m, negativity strength α, and asymmetry parameters
phase_3.true_description: verification passed — the operator set satisfies the current AI-NOVM property being checked; the tool advances to the next verification stage or to output generation
phase_3.false_description: verification failed — the operator set does not satisfy the checked AI-NOVM property; the measurement is either a standard POVM (all eigenvalues nonnegative), tomographically complete (m ≥ d²), or symmetric (nontrivial group action)
phase_3.both_description: the quasi-probability distribution — simultaneously true as a normalized measurement outcome (∑p_i = 1) and false as a classical probability distribution (some p_i < 0); this dialetheic state is held without resolution throughout the computation

steps.domain_action: the tool starts in void state — no parameters for dimension d, outcome count m, negativity strength α, or asymmetry vector have been loaded
the normalization constraint ∑E_i = I_d is established as the closed boundary — every subsequent operator construction must resolve the identity exactly

load construction parameters — read dimension d (2 through 8), outcome count m (< d² for incompleteness), negativity strength α (determining the spread of eigenvalues below zero), and asymmetry parameters (distinct spectral profiles per operator)
decompose the identity — split I_d into m Hermitian operators {E_1, ..., E_m} constructed from the generalized Gell-Mann basis using the parameterized formula, ensuring ∑E_i = I_d by design
verify Hermiticity of each operator — check E_i† = E_i for all i from 1 to m, confirming each operator is self-adjoint and eligible for real-valued quasi-probability computation
load the input quantum state — accept either a pure state vector |ψ⟩ ∈ ℂ^d or a density matrix ρ as the measurement target
compute quasi-probabilities via Born rule — evaluate p_i = Tr(ρE_i) for each i, producing the m-dimensional quasi-probability vector
begin negativity verification — check whether any E_i possesses a strictly negative eigenvalue
decompose each E_i spectrally — compute E_i = U_i Λ_i U_i†, extracting the minimal eigenvalue λ_min(i) and the full spectrum spec(E_i)
negativity confirmed — min_i λ_min(E_i) < 0, the measurement contains at least one operator with a negative eigenvalue, satisfying the NOVM condition
negativity absent — all λ_min(E_i) ≥ 0, every operator is positive semidefinite, the measurement is a standard POVM not an NOVM
verify information-incompleteness — check whether the outcome count m is strictly less than d²
incompleteness confirmed — m < d², the operators span a proper subspace of the d²-dimensional operator space, the measurement is information-incomplete
incompleteness absent — m ≥ d², the operators span the full operator space, the measurement is tomographically complete
verify asymmetry — compare all m spectra pairwise to check whether any two operators share the same eigenvalue multiset
asymmetry confirmed — all m spectra {spec(E_i)} are pairwise distinct, no unitary or antiunitary conjugation maps any operator to another, the measurement is asymmetric
asymmetry absent — at least two operators share identical spectra, indicating a symmetry group action permuting effects, the measurement possesses nontrivial symmetry

hold the quasi-probability paradice — the vector (p_1, ..., p_m) is acknowledged as both a valid normalized measurement (∑p_i = 1 from the NOVM boundary) and an invalid classical distribution (negative entries present); this dialetheic state is the signature of the NOVM
sum the operators back to identity — compute ∑_{i=1}^m E_i, recovering I_d exactly, closing the Frobenius pair with the original identity decomposition
prepare grammar pipeline integration — construct the JSON output structure linking to the catalog entry asymmetric_ai_novm with tuple ⟨𐑨𐑰𐑽𐑗𐑐𐑪𐑲𐑠𐑢𐑒𐑳𐑷⟩

write the permanent JSON output — the quasi-probability vector, negativity score N(ρ) = (∑|p_i| − 1)/2, verification results with per-property pass/fail flags, operator spectra, and grammar tuple are irreversibly recorded for downstream consumption
